questions.cardText:
[Astronomy] How does the Moon look different based on where you are on Earth?
A. You see different orientations
B. You see a different side of the Moon
C. You see a different size
Answer: A. In the northern hemisphere, the Moon appears “upside down” compared to its appearance in the southern hemisphere.
questions.de: Wie erscheint der Mond einem Beobachter auf der Südhalbkugel im Vergleich zu seinem Anblick von der Nordhalbkugel?
questions.en: How does the Moon appear to an observer in the Southern Hemisphere compared with its look from the Northern Hemisphere?

source.title: Can the Moon be upside down? — The Planetary Society

questions.notes: Everyone sees the same (near) side; only its orientation differs (rotated about 180°). Near the equator the orientation changes through the night. The fact has no date of its own, so the timeline shows the Moon's formation.

questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Which of the following animals is known to have unique names for individuals within their group?
A. Dolphins
B. Naked mole rats
C. Hyenas
Answer: A. Dolphins use unique whistles to identify and call each other, much like how humans use names. Besides dolphins, elephants and parrots can also audibly identify unique individuals.
questions.de: Welche Meeressäuger erkennen und rufen einander mit individuell unverwechselbaren „Signaturpfiffen“, ähnlich wie mit Namen?
questions.en: Which marine mammals identify and call one another with individually distinctive “signature whistles”, much like names?

timeline.labelEn: Melba and David Caldwell describe individually distinctive whistles in bottlenose dolphins
timeline.labelDe: Melba und David Caldwell beschreiben individuell unterschiedliche Pfiffe bei Großen Tümmlern

questions.notes: Signature whistles are best documented in bottlenose dolphins (first described by Caldwell & Caldwell, Nature 1965).
